ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, managers, and ultimate beneficial owners against the Luxembourg FIU list, EU consolidated sanctions list, UN Security Council sanctions, OFAC/SDN list, and domestic PEP registers; risk-based customer due diligence under the Law of 17 May 2018 and CSSF AML circulars; enhanced due diligence is triggered by high-risk jurisdictions, complex cross-border structures, or material transactions through non-banking rails.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) electronic platform (LBR / eJustice portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Latin script; French, German, or Luxembourgish names are preferred; non-Latin names require an exact Latin transliteration; the legal form suffix 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL' must appear; names must not be misleading, identical, or confusingly similar to an existing registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within one month from the rejection notice, file a written administrative appeal with the Director of the Luxembourg Business Registers; include the original name-reservation reference, the proposed corrective name, and legal grounds; if the administrative refusal is upheld, a judicial appeal may be lodged with the Luxembourg administrative tribunal within three months; no extension of the reservation window exists, but a fresh reservation may be filed after paying the applicable fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual address is not acceptable as the sole registered office; the SARL must maintain a physical registered office in Luxembourg and retain sufficient local administrative substance; a licensed domiciliation agent may be used provided actual management and operational activities are conducted from Luxembourg.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 5% annual baseline probability of unannounced physical on-site inspection for a low-risk consultancy; the probability increases materially if AML red flags, misrepresentations, unusual cross-border transaction volumes, or substance deficiencies are identified.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales); Title I and Articles 100-112 governing the Société à Responsabilité Limitée; Law of 2 September 2011 on the access to regulated professions, where applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), with e-filing available via www.lbr.lu and the Guichet.lu portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif – notarial deed of incorporation containing the articles of association (statuts), filed with the RCS for registration and publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and fully paid in cash. The capital must be deposited into a blocked bank account (compte bloqué) with a Luxembourg credit institution before notarial execution, and a blocked-funds certificate must be obtained. The funds are released only after RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED FIRST MEETING OF FOUNDERS: 1) The subscription of the entire share capital of EUR 12,000, represented by 12,000 shares of EUR 1 each, is confirmed and accepted as fully paid. 2) The registered office is established at [Address], Luxembourg, and the manager is authorised to execute the lease and notify the RCS. 3) [Name], born [date], resident at [Address], is appointed sole gérant of the company, with power to represent the company, open bank accounts, and execute all registration and tax formalities. 4) All pre-incorporation acts and expenses are ratified. Passed unanimously by all founders.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name clearance and residential address validation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary, in consultation with the RCS name database through Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the notary to run a name availability search and validate that the proposed corporate name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name. The notary also verifies that the proposed registered office address is physically usable and admissible under Luxembourg corporate law. The notary prepares a draft deed of incorporation including an accurate ISIC 7020 corporate purpose covering overseas market-entry consulting.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of each founder and designated manager
Proof of residential address (utility bill or occupancy certificate)
Three proposed company names in order of preference
Draft articles of association and corporate purpose clause
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, submit the next alternative from the preference list; if the registered office address lacks documentary proof, provide a draft notarial lease or letter of accommodation from the owner to cure the file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of blocked capital account and deposit of minimum capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution selected by the founders (e.g., Banque Internationale à Luxembourg, Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État, or BGL BNP Paribas).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the name of the future SARL. Deposit at least EUR 12,000 and obtain a blocked-funds certificate (attestation de blocage). The certificate must be issued not earlier than five working days before the notarial execution and must state that the funds irrevocably remain at the disposal of the future company until registration.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association
Passport and due-diligence identification of all shareholders and beneficial owners
Anti-money laundering / know-your-customer declaration
Source-of-funds statement and bank reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the AML file, resubmit corrected and notarially certified identification documents; if the blocked-funds certificate is delayed, escalate to the bank's corporate services desk or obtain a certified bank undertaking dated not more than three banking days before signing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of notarial deed of incorporation and publication preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary duly admitted to the notarial profession.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Attend a notarial appointment with all founders or their authorised attorneys-in-fact. The notary reads the deed, confirms the payment of capital with the blocked-funds certificate, verifies the identity and capacity of signatories, and receives signatures on the constitutive act. The notary then files the deed with the RCS and causes the legal notice to be prepared for publication in RESA.
required_dossiers: Blocked-funds certificate from the Luxembourg bank
Notarial draft of the articles of association
Original passports or IDs of all signatories
Power of attorney, if any signatory is acting through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a founder fails to appear, the notary may require a certified power of attorney; if a formal defect is found during signature review, the notary prepares a rectification deed and the founders re-sign without losing priority in the RCS queue.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and issuance of the company matricule
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), online portal lbr.lu.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary submits the full registration file electronically through the secure RCS portal. The RCS checks compliance with the Law of 10 August 1915, validates the articles, and issues the official registration certificate (extrait) and the 12-digit matricule number. The company acquires legal personality upon registration.
required_dossiers: Notarial deed of incorporation
Blocked-funds certificate of the subscribed capital
RCS standard form C (coordinated filing information)
Beneficial ownership declaration for filing with the RBE
Proof of payment of the RCS registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query identifying missing annexes, the notary file a supplementary filing within eight working days; any correction is made without re-execution of the deed, unless the defect affects the statutory minimum capital or the corporate object.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate governance, tax, and social security registration of the SARL
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Luxembourg Business Registers for RBE; Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the first board resolution adopting the registered office and appointing the gérant in the corporate records. File the beneficial ownership declaration through the RBE portal. Register the company for corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and Luxembourg VAT with AEDT. Register the gérant and any employees for social security with CCSS.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate and matricule
First board resolution approving officers and registered office
Original passports of the gérant and any authorised signatories
Lease contract for the registered office
VAT registration form (Formulaire A - AEDT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEDT requests additional economic substance information, provide a formalised business plan and projected financials; if the RBE declaration is refused due to incomplete data, correct the beneficial ownership grid and resubmit before any transaction is carried out.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Occupational, fire safety, and environmental clearance for office operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local commune (municipality) services for building compliance; Service Incendie et Secours (SDIS); Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM); Administration de l'Environnement.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a fire safety conformity inspection for the registered office and any workstations occupied by staff. If the company rents an office unit, the landlord or tenant obtains the commune fire-safety certificate. For office-based consultancy, file an ITM declaration of workplace when the first employee is hired. No environmental operating permit is required, but an authorised waste-collection contract must be in place for office refuse. If no industrial equipment is installed, no structural load study is necessary.
required_dossiers: Registered office lease or ownership title
Commune fire-safety inspection certificate or SDIS inspection report
ITM workplace declaration (if employees are engaged)
Waste disposal contract with an authorised carrier
Building occupancy permit if the office premises require a change of use
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire-safety inspection requires remediation works, perform the works and request a reinspection; if ITM notifies a breach of occupational duties, submit the missing declaration or apply for partial exemption for a small office under Article 2 of the Labour Code.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no industrial or manufacturing licensing authority applies to ISIC 7020 overseas market-entry consulting. For general business formalities, the competent authorities are the Ministry of Economy, the local commune, and the RCS.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating, manufacturing, or commercial permit is required for a Luxembourg SARL engaged exclusively in management consultancy services under ISIC 7020.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – office-based consultancy activity does not trigger an environmental impact assessment or environmental classed-establishment permit under the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental assessment and the amended classement regulation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOCs, or significant air emissions are generated. Office refuse must be segregated and collected by an authorised waste operator in compliance with the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management; any cooling equipment must comply with the EU F-gas Regulation (EU) No. 517/2014 regarding refrigerant leakage checks.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance of the registered office and any administrative workspace is required from the local commune upon SDIS inspection; occupational health and safety declaration to ITM is required for any employee workstations; no structural load inspection applies to normal office occupancy.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct corporate income tax and municipal business tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for registration duties and VAT; e-government portal Guichet.lu / MyGuichet.lu, with dedicated e-TVA electronic filing and the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR / RCS) company registry.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign parent establishing a Luxembourg SARL must (i) execute the bylaws before a notary and file with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), which automatically issues the 13-digit national business registration number (numéro matricule) used uniformly for corporate income tax, municipal business tax, net wealth tax and social security references; (ii) file the VAT registration application (form 010) with the AEDT through MyGuichet.lu, after which the authority issues a Luxembourg VAT identification number in the format LU followed by eight digits; (iii) where the foreign entity has no permanent establishment in Luxembourg and makes taxable supplies in Luxembourg, VAT registration from the first euro is mandatory unless the reverse charge shifts liability to the customer or an OSS/IOSS scheme applies; (iv) opening a corporate bank account at a Luxembourg or EU credit institution is a practical precondition for obtaining inward remittance evidence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Luxembourg SARL is a resident company taxable at entity level on worldwide income, subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax, while qualifying dividends and capital gains benefit from the participation exemption regime; the SARL is not a pass-through entity and has no US-style check-the-box capacity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg law does not provide a check-the-box election. Statutory elections available to a SARL include: (a) fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) under Article 164bis LIR for corporate income tax, available where a Luxembourg parent directly holds at least 95% of the SARL and each consolidated Luxembourg subsidiary; (b) VAT group registration under Article 61 of the Luxembourg VAT Law, allowing jointly liable VAT consolidation of Luxembourg establishments; (c) waiver of the small-enterprise VAT exemption under Article 57 of the VAT Law to enter the normal VAT system and deduct input VAT; (d) EU OSS/IOSS options for cross-border distance sales and B2C electronic services; (e) ATAD hybrid-mismatch alignments, with mandatory recharacterisation of deductible payments producing double-non-taxation outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA) under Council Directive 2006/112/EC as transposed by the Luxembourg VAT Law (loi modifiée du 12 février 1979).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000: Luxembourg domestic small-enterprise exemption threshold under Article 57 of the VAT Law for resident taxable persons with annual taxable turnover not exceeding EUR 35,000; registration becomes mandatory when the threshold is exceeded, when intra-EU acquisitions exceed EUR 10,000, or for non-established foreign suppliers from the first euro of taxable Luxembourg supply unless the reverse charge or OSS/IOSS applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg currently imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, e-invoicing API mandate, or digital stamping for domestic VAT. Electronic invoicing is accepted provided the authenticity and integrity of the invoice are guaranteed; Peppol and Factur-X are permitted voluntarily. Mandatory digitalisation applies to (i) electronic VAT return filing and payment through the e-TVA portal by companies subject to corporate income tax, and (ii) electronic lodging of customs/export declarations with the Luxembourg Customs and Excise Agency through the EU Automated Export System (AES) and the national single window (myguichet.lu / LU-CIS), with an MRN evidenced on each exported consignment.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Two distinct pathways apply to a Luxembourg SARL providing overseas market-entry consultancy: (1) B2B services: consultancy services are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT and thus effectively zero-rated where the customer is a taxable person established in a third country and the general B2B place-of-supply rule under Article 58 of the VAT Directive (transposed at Articles 34-35 of the Luxembourg VAT Law) places the supply in the customer's jurisdiction; the Luxembourg 'use and enjoyment' carve-out may nonetheless re-characterise the supply as taxable in Luxembourg when the services are effectively used and enjoyed in Luxembourg. (2) Goods: physical exports of goods (e.g., printed market reports or regulatory deliverables) qualify for the 0% rate under Article 43 of the Luxembourg VAT Law only where the goods are consigned to a destination outside the European Union and the exporter retains full documentary proof of physical export. Zero-rating remains conditional on proper books and records, and input VAT attributable to zero-rated or outside-scope supplies remains creditable in full or pro rata under the normal deduction rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration: Single Administrative Document (DAU) or electronic declaration lodged with the Luxembourg Customs and Excise Agency through the EU Automated Export System, including the Movement Reference Number (MRN) and export acceptance record evidencing EU exit.

Bill of Lading or airway bill (or CMR consignment note for road freight) showing the Luxembourg exporter as consignor and the named third-country destination, with carrier date stamp or electronic event log.
Inward Remittance Certificate: bank credit advice, SWIFT MT103, or a confirmation issued by a Luxembourg or EU paying bank evidencing receipt of export consideration in convertible currency.
Commercial invoice containing explicit zero-rating wording, Incoterms rule, country of destination, and a detailed breakdown of consultancy fees and deliverables.
Executed consultancy agreement or engagement letter together with feasibility reports, progress correspondence, and time records substantiating the overseas market-entry services actually rendered.
Foreign customer taxable-status evidence, such as an overseas business registry certificate or a foreign VAT/GST identification number, to support the B2B zero-rated treatment.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT rigorously audits zero-rated and export-exempt supplies; where the documentary evidence bundle is missing, incomplete, or false, the supply is re-characterised as taxable in Luxembourg and 17% VAT is assessed on the gross consideration, plus late-payment interest under the General Tax Law (Abgabenordnung) at 0.6% per month and an evasion supplement of up to the full amount of the evaded tax. Intentional or materially false zero-rating declarations constitute VAT fraud under Articles 55-64 of the Luxembourg VAT Law and Articles 25-28 of the General Tax Law, exposing the SARL and its directors to criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 in aggravated cases, confiscation orders, and custodial sentences of up to five years. The standard reassessment limitation is five years, extended to ten years for fraudulent or concealed facts.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) and Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). The BCL is the monetary, payments and statistical authority; the CSSF is the licensing, prudential and AML/CFT supervisor for banks. Luxembourg has no separate foreign-exchange administration or exchange-control licensing body.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for residents and non-residents, and Luxembourg applies the EU free-movement-of-capital rules (Article 63 TFEU). Capital-account and current-account operations are unrestricted; no exchange-control authorization, currency-transaction permit, or profit-repatriation license is required. Profit remittance is constrained only by ordinary company-law distribution tests (balance-sheet test, legal reserve, and going-concern test) and by any applicable withholding tax; once the SARL has fulfilled those tests, dividends can be paid freely by wire. All transfers remain subject to EU asset-freeze/sanctions regulations and to BCL balance-of-payments reporting obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export-proceeds repatriation, surrender, or mandatory conversion rules for the euro area/Luxembourg. A Luxembourg SARL may retain export receivables in a foreign-currency account or convert them into euro at the bank rate. The only routine regulatory requirement is statistical reporting to the BCL: payments received from non-residents, or sent to non-residents, must be declared by the SARL or by its bank through the national balance-of-payments reporting system when the transaction exceeds the applicable de minimis threshold. No conversion percentage is imposed.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Contribution (Blocked) Account / Operational Treasury Account
Capital Escrow Account / Operational EUR-USD Account
Operational Treasury Account and Cross-Border Trade/FX Facility

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Digital Payment Platform

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium as an ancillary settlement rail; Low as the sole treasury rail. EEA-licensed electronic-money institutions (EMIs) and payment-service providers are permitted in Luxembourg through the European passport under PSD2/EMD2 and may be used for low-value fee collections, multi-currency current accounts and the 'Wise_B2B' rails available to the client. Legal constraints: an EMI cannot grant credit, issue commercial letters of credit, enter into derivative contracts, or hold client funds in a deposit-guarantee-protected account; client funds must be safeguarded, not lent. Therefore the SARL must maintain a principal relationship with a Luxembourg or EEA licensed credit institution for trade settlements, FX hedging and subscription-capital custody.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: As a general rule, at least one natural-person managing director (gérant) and each 25% or more beneficial owner must attend a face-to-face KYC interview before a tier-1 Luxembourg bank will open a corporate account; this is a risk-based requirement driven by CSSF AML/CFT circulars and the Law of 12 November 2004. Remote opening via certified video identification is allowed by most tier-1 banks for a low-risk consultancy SARL, but it is frequently provisional and conditional on the subsequent physical signature of the banking agreement at a Luxembourg branch or consular/notarial legalization. If no director is physically present, the bank will normally require a Luxembourg-resident authorized signatory, a notarized power of attorney, or a certified copy of the passport plus apostilled corporate documents. The blocked capital-subscription account in particular is generally opened only after an in-person instruction to the notary or bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO chain passes through an offshore entity located in a FATF/EU-grey-listed jurisdiction or with no demonstrable economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified constitutional documents and good-standing certificates for each chain entity; updated UBO register extract or sworn UBO declaration; group organigram with percentage interests; substance evidence (lease, payroll, active bank account, local filings); audited financial statements for every material entity; transfer-pricing documentation; source-of-wealth statement for the ultimate shareholder; legal opinion from counsel in the residence jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: One of the beneficial owners or directors is a Politically Exposed Person (PEP) or has an unexplained high-risk PEP history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP declaration form; detailed source-of-funds and source-of-wealth file; independent asset verification; official tax clearance certificates; audited accounts; explanation of the commercial rationale for the market-entry consultancy; senior compliance committee approval memorandum and the bank's enhanced monitoring plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction pattern is inconsistent with the stated ISIC 7020 advisory business, for example same-day mirror flows, payments to commodity intermediaries, or layered jurisdiction hops without invoice-specific explanations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Originals of signed advisory/service contracts and milestones; invoice-by-invoice reconciliation; evidence of actual delivery of market-feasibility or regulatory-licensing work; CVs, staffing and functional organization chart; general ledger and treasury policy; a written explanation of the payment chain; tax filings and BCL balance-of-payments reports confirming services classification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions-related concern: counterparties, banks, IP addresses or routing codes linked to sanctioned states, entities or individuals.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening results for all parties and authorized signatories; bank statements validating the commercial origin of funds; legal opinion under EU and Luxembourg sanctions laws; certification that the consultancy does not provide management or technology services to embargoed sectors; monitoring plan for future sanctioned-entity detection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient commercial substance in Luxembourg: no physical office, no full-time employees and minimal local expenditures for a non-resident-managed SARL.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement and office photographs where applicable; employment agreements or alternative service agreements; Luxembourg VAT and corporate tax returns demonstrating substance; local regulatory license statement noting that ISIC 7020 does not require a statutory license; board minutes evidencing real decision-making in Luxembourg; business plan and expected revenue projections.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For initial share capital, route a SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA Credit Transfer for euro if from an EU account) to the SARL's formation or blocked account at the chosen Luxembourg bank. The beneficiary account name must exactly match the notarial deed and bank reference; the MT103 narrative should state 'direct investment – subscription of share capital in LU_SARL'. The bank will classify the inbound remittance for BCL balance-of-payments purposes under direct investment, inward equity capital, not as a trade or service payment. Required verification package: notarized articles of association, RCS or registration reference, shareholder identification and source-of-funds evidence, proof of full payment of the subscribed capital, and the completed bank KYC file. No CSSF consent is required solely for the capital route; the funds remain blocked until the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) files the incorporation deed. For subsequent intra-group loans or additional paid-in capital, the purpose code should reflect intercompany financing and, if material, a cross-border intra-group loan agreement and pricing benchmark must be supplied.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The SARL should use SWIFT MT103 for direct cross-border client-facing settlements in EUR or USD and for paying foreign contractors; documentary trade settlements are executed through Commercial Letters of Credit (sight or usance) opened by the bank and governed by UCP600 and ISBP745; import collections and documentary collections may also be used. Within the EEA, ordinary operational disbursements clear via SEPA Credit Transfer; high-value USD cross-border clearing uses SWIFT, CHIPS or the bank's correspondent network. Treasury disbursements must include BCL balance-of-payments reporting and sanction screening of every beneficiary, and the bank must append an accurate purpose code (services, direct investment or financial investment) to avoid regulatory misstatement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright forward foreign-exchange contracts (EUR/USD and EUR/non-EUR) with delivery on the contracted settlement date, documented as hedge-accounting instruments.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted emerging-market currencies that have no liquid onshore forward market, cash-settled at an agreed fixing source and approved by the bank's risk desk.
Foreign-exchange swaps combining a spot and reverse forward transaction for managing funding mismatches and intercompany loan rollovers.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps for long-term foreign-currency assets or loans, executed under an ISDA and CSA framework.
European-style plain vanilla FX options purchased for downside-rate protection, with no barrier, binary or speculative credit enhancers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS data confirmation (confirmation annuelle) of commercial register particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Every calendar year by 31 March; material changes to RCS-listed particulars must also be filed within one month of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted confirmation leaves the RCS record stale; subsequent filings may be refused, and the LBR may impose fines under applicable business-register rules. Persistent non-confirmation can lead to the RCS removing the SARL from the register through an administrative strike-off procedure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (annual accounts) deposit and publication
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after the end of the financial year; for a calendar-year SARL, no later than 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file annual accounts is punishable by administrative fines up to EUR 5,000, and the accounts may be filed under judicial compulsion. Repeated non-filing permits the Public Prosecutor to apply to the commercial court for compulsory winding-up and deregistration from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual combined tax return for corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally by 31 May of the year following the tax year; extensions may be granted by the ACD on written request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a penalty of EUR 250 per month or fraction thereof (minimum EUR 100), plus late-payment interest of 0.6% per month. The ACD may assess the SARL ex officio from factual information and enforce collection against assets where the SARL continues to default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership confirmation and UBO register declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March; any transfer of shares or change in beneficial ownership must be filed with the RBE within one month after the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliant UBO filings are subject to administrative fines and criminal sanctions under the Luxembourg UBO law. Continued non-filing may be recorded on the RBE file, restrict subsequent corporate actions, and serve as an independent ground for RCS strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SARL must appoint an independent statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) when it exceeds two of the three following thresholds at the balance sheet date: balance-sheet total EUR 4.4 million, annual net turnover EUR 8.8 million, and average workforce of 50 employees. Public-interest entities, credit institutions, insurance undertakings and certain CSSF-regulated companies require an audit regardless of size; a small SARL is otherwise exempt.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Annual accounts are prepared in euros under Luxembourg GAAP (Lux GAAP) and the Luxembourg Commercial Code. Listed companies must use IFRS for statutory accounts; unlisted companies may apply IFRS electively under the conditions of the Commercial Code.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every SARL must file a UBO declaration with the RBE within one month of incorporation and must confirm the exactness of the beneficial ownership data between 1 January and 31 March of each calendar year. Any transfer of registered shares, or any movement crossing the 25% ownership or control threshold, requires a fresh RBE filing within one month. The declaration identifies each natural person owning or controlling, directly or indirectly, more than 25% of the share capital or voting rights or exercising other means of control; unresolved UBO details must be documented in the SARL's internal AML compliance file.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of managers and management resolutions (procès-verbaux des gérants)
Register of minutes of shareholders' general meetings
Internal documentation and transfer records supporting the annual UBO confirmation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500–USD 1,200 per year for registered office and status-keeping; USD 1,500–USD 4,000 per year for a Luxembourg corporate administrator or RCS filing agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000–USD 18,000 for a small SARL statutory audit when thresholds are exceeded; a lighter réviseur d'entreprises review for a below-threshold SARL is typically USD 2,000–USD 5,000

stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
